Subject: Dedicated entitlement scaling proposal for Cygnus — throughput & headroom

Hi Eva,

Thanks again for taking the time last week. Per our discussion I pulled together a proposal that maps your expected request mix to a dedicated slab sizing and the estimated headroom for p95 token latency at three traffic tiers. The attached Cygnus_MAAP_v2.xlsx has the workbook; the short version below.

Summary assumptions (from your intake):
- Avg prompt length: 210 tokens; avg response length: 380 tokens (total ~590 tokens per call)
- Burst pattern: 3x baseline during business hours for 4 x 30-min windows per day
- Model: redwood-titan-xl-16k (quantized q4f16 profile)

Proposal highlights:
- Baseline entitlement: 120k tokens/sec sustained (matches your mid-season run rate)
- Committed slab: 1.5x baseline (180k tokens/sec) to retain p95 <= 450ms with 25% operational headroom
- Burst credit pool + autoscale cap to 3x baseline for limited windows (pre-warmed cache)

Next steps I recommend:
1) Engineering validation call (30 min) to walk the per-model tokens/sec numbers — Ben + Karthik to join.
2) Procurement review of SLA redlines — I attached an initial redline draft (SLA-draft-redlines.pdf).
3) If the sizing looks good, we convert to a 12-month reserved slab with quarterly traffic checkpoints.

Can Ben join the engineering call tomorrow at 11am PT? I copied Karthik for the model-level numbers.

Best,
Camila

Hi all — quick engineering note with the numbers we'll show in the call. Summary (redwood-titan-xl-16k, q4f16):
- Single GPU sustained throughput (in our bench, median): ~38k tokens/sec for 590-token interactions (batching profile B2).
- Practical issuing limit (to keep p95 <= 450ms): 32k tokens/sec per GPU at target concurrency and small-batch latency mode.
- Cache warming: prefix/KV cache reduces effective per-call work by ~18% after hot paths; we recommend a warmed pool for your predictable morning spikes.

Sizing math to justify 1.5x commit:
- Requested baseline: 120k tokens/sec => 120k / 32k ~= 3.75 GPUs => round up to 4 GPUs for baseline headroom.
- 1.5x committed slab => 180k tokens/sec => 180k / 32k ~= 5.6 GPUs => provision 6 GPUs.
- Effective operational headroom at 180k: ~25% (accounting for KV cache, slower tails, maintenance windows).

For the 4x sustained 20-min burst scenario: 4x baseline = 480k tokens/sec => 480k / 32k = 15 GPUs. We recommend a hybrid model: reserve 6 GPUs (committed) + pre-approved burst pool of up to 10 additional GPUs with 30-min pre-warm window. That keeps p95 below 800ms for short bursts and avoids provisioned overcommit for rare extremes.

I'll bring these exact numbers to the engineering call.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Inference Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Pricing options for Cygnus — reserved slab vs. committed headroom

Eva / Procurement team — attaching the two pricing options as promised:
A) 12-month reserved slab at 6 GPUs (180k tokens/sec) — $XX,XXX/month, includes 25% operational headroom, 4:1 burst credits for limited windows (pre-warm required).
B) 12-month committed + burst pool: 4 GPUs reserved (120k tokens/sec) + credit to burst up to additional 10 GPUs on-demand at a higher unit rate; lower monthly commitment (~$YY,YYY/month) but higher marginal burst costs.

We modeled cost-per-token under both to show breakeven at different burst frequencies — see Cygnus_MAAP_v2.xlsx tab 'pricing-sim'. If your bursts run >60 minutes/day averaged over the month, option A is more cost-effective.

We can convert whichever option you prefer into a PO-ready quote; Camila will coordinate final SLA language.
